Share on X Telegram Investors’ sell-offs wiped N2.99 trillion off the Nigerian stock market last week as profit-taking activities following weeks of strong gains triggered a decline in share prices across several counters.
The benchmark Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) All-Share Index (ASI) fell by 1.83 per cent week-on-week to close at 247,660.74 points, while market capitalisation declined by approximately N2.99 trillion to N160.80 trillion.
Consequently, the market’s year-to-date (YTD) return moderated to 59.15 per cent, reflecting the impact of sustained selling pressure on equities. Market sentiment remained weak throughout the week, with market breadth closing negative as 43 stocks declined against 39 gainers, indicating that losses outnumbered advances across the trading floor.
Livingtrust Mortgage Bank led the gainers’ table with a 28.76 per cent appreciation to close at N3.00 per share. Chellarams followed with a 20.62 per cent gain to close at N11.70, while International Breweries advanced by 20.24 per cent to close at N10.10 per share.
On the losers’ table, Meyer led with a 17.43 per cent decline to close at N14.45 per share. R.T. Briscoe followed with a 16.94 per cent loss to close at N7.60, while Lasaco Assurance shed 10 per cent to close at N1.71 per share.
Trading activity also weakened during the week, as investors exchanged 2.366 billion shares valued at N106.363 billion in 159,759 deals, compared with 8.029 billion shares worth N185.358 billion traded in 160,836 deals in the preceding week.
The decline in trading volume and value underscored the cautious disposition of investors amid persistent profit-taking and weakening market sentiment.
Market analysts, however, described the weekly decline as a healthy correction following the market’s sustained rally, rather than an indication of a fundamental downturn.
They noted that profit-taking was expected after an extended period of gains, as investors sought to lock in returns and rebalance their portfolios.
However, they cautioned that market sentiment remained fragile, with investors closely monitoring macroeconomic indicators, corporate earnings, interest rate movements and foreign exchange developments for fresh direction.
On the market outlook, Sterling Asset Management and Trustees Limited (SAMTL) said the recovery of the equities market would depend largely on renewed investor confidence and buying interest.
“The market’s recovery will depend on renewed investor confidence and buying interest. However, continued selling may cause further short-term declines, while lower share prices could attract new buyers,” the firm stated.
Similarly, Cowry Assets Management Limited projected cautious trading in the coming week, warning that persistent profit-taking and weak investor sentiment could continue to weigh on market performance.
The firm, however, noted that the relatively resilient performance of the insurance and consumer goods sectors could provide some support to the market.
